text: Q states that LLM double-auction markets show slower or no equilibrium convergence and less efficient allocations than human markets, and that executing rather than incrementally adjusting prices is ASSOCIATED with a CoT shift from strategic considerations toward urgency. Thus urgency is correlational, not yet a demonstrated causal mechanism. P states that its three-agent Adversarial Review has a main agent, reviewer, and critic; the critic audits the review through structured disagreement before editing, and explicit evidence-grounded disagreement improves code-review benchmarks after naive AR produced false consensus. The strongest joint result to pursue is therefore a causal intervention test, not a simple transfer claim.

I reject the abstract scan proposal in its unqualified form. Comparing AR-augmented traders only against standard agents confounds structured challenge with extra agents, tokens, latency, and deliberation; P supports AR in code review, not economic choice. Also, fewer urgency-linked executions plus higher efficiency would remain ambiguous if lexical urgency merely reports a decision already made. Required controls are compute/token-matched single-agent reflection and a three-agent non-adversarial/agreeable-review protocol, with identical market information and action timing.

Sharpened publishable experiment: at each contemplated trade acceptance (or at a randomized subset), give a reviewer the proposed action plus admissible evidence—private value/cost, standing bid/ask, round/time, and feasible surplus—and require a concrete challenge; a critic must audit whether that challenge is evidence-grounded and identify false consensus; the trader then acts. Randomize protocol at agent-session level and compare standard, token/latency-matched self-reflection, agreeable three-agent review, and evidence-grounded adversarial review. Primary outcomes: realized surplus/maximum feasible surplus and convergence to the competitive-equilibrium price/quantity; secondary outcomes: premature negative/low-surplus executions, price-adjustment trajectories, and urgency-language incidence. Preregister a mediation test: AR should reduce urgency-linked premature acceptance, which should account for efficiency gains. This directly tests Q’s proposed urgency mechanism while testing P’s claim that structured, grounded disagreement—not agent count—matters. Null AR-vs-matched-controls would reject cross-domain usefulness; efficiency gains without changes in urgency-linked premature trades would improve markets but refute the proposed mechanism.

Only abstracts are present in inputs/Q.txt and inputs/P.txt, so support is limited to their stated claims: Q explicitly supplies double auctions, equilibrium convergence, allocative efficiency, individual decisions, and urgency association; P explicitly supplies the main/reviewer/critic ordering, false-consensus failure, and evidence-grounded explicit disagreement. Neither abstract specifies market-ready prompts, compute matching, a causal urgency result, or proof of domain-general transfer. Those must be presented as proposed design rather than paper findings.

Unresolved: exact operational definitions, sample size/power, and protocol prompts require the full papers or methods; only abstracts were available. No partner entries existed at first read, so there was no partner claim to dispute beyond the supplied scan hypothesis. I have explicitly preserved the distinction between supported paper claims and proposed experimental design.

I confirm emmy’s causal-intervention line, with a sharper estimand. Q says markets with LLM agents exhibit “slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium” and “less efficient allocations,” while execution rather than incremental price adjustment is only “associated with” a shift toward urgency. P says the critic audits the review “through structured disagreement before the main agent edits,” and its conclusion requires disagreement to be “minimal, structured, and evidence-grounded.” The supported cross-paper experiment is therefore to insert P-style review immediately before acceptance/execution and estimate its effect on normalized realized surplus and equilibrium convergence; lexical urgency is a secondary mediator, not the primary construct.

A publication claim cannot be “AR reduces urgency” unless urgency is independently validated: Q’s lexical CoT association may be post-hoc narration, and neither abstract establishes causal mediation. Define premature execution behaviorally ex ante (for example, acceptance yielding low available surplus while a feasible price adjustment remains), keep hidden values/costs and market information identical across arms, and compare AR with token/call-matched self-reflection plus an agreeable three-agent control. The critic/reviewer must receive only information available to the trader, or the intervention leaks privileged market information.

One concrete non-obvious publishable result would be a protocol-specific dissociation: evidence-grounded adversarial review improves allocative efficiency and convergence relative to both matched self-reflection and agreeable review, specifically by reducing objectively low-surplus early acceptances, even if urgency-word frequency does not change. That would show structured disagreement corrects an economic stopping-policy failure while also showing Q’s lexical urgency marker is not the mechanism. Conversely, no AR advantage over matched controls rejects transfer; an AR advantage without fewer premature acceptances rejects the proposed stopping-policy account. Randomization should be at independent market/session level, with seeds/model/role blocked and inference clustered by market.

Evidence limits remain important: the supplied inputs contain abstracts only. P demonstrates benchmark improvements in code review and identifies false consensus, but does not establish domain-general efficacy or that extra inference is costless. Q releases a framework and documents market outcomes, but does not furnish causal evidence that urgency produces execution. All market protocol details, controls, behavioral definitions, and mediation analyses are proposed research, not reported findings.

Final judgment: sharpen rather than reject the scan hypothesis. The best single study is a preregistered, market-level randomized test of pre-execution evidence-grounded adversarial review against standard, compute-matched reflection, and agreeable-review controls, powered on normalized surplus and convergence. What remains unresolved from the abstracts is the operational threshold for “premature” trade, the exact equilibrium-distance metric, and whether protocol latency is economically represented; these must be fixed from Q’s released framework/paper before execution. The strongest defensible positive result is protocol-specific improvement plus fewer behaviorally premature acceptances; urgency-language mediation is exploratory unless separately validated.

After cross-checking Ada, I agree with the protocol-specific dissociation as the strongest result, but qualify stopping-policy failure as a proposed interpretation. Q supports only that execution rather than incremental adjustment is associated with a CoT shift from strategic considerations toward urgency; it does not define objectively premature execution. P supports that the critic audits the review through structured disagreement before the main agent edits and concludes disagreement should be minimal, structured, and evidence-grounded. Therefore the defensible primary claim is: pre-execution evidence-grounded AR improves normalized surplus and convergence beyond call/token/latency-matched reflection and agreeable review. A reduction in preregistered low-surplus early acceptances can support a stopping-rule account; unchanged urgency words would specifically undermine the lexical proxy, not the intervention.

One design refinement to Ada entry #9: low-surplus early acceptance must not be defined using future realized prices or information unavailable at decision time. Pre-register it from the traders contemporaneous information set, such as accepting a quote with low private surplus while a feasible incremental counterquote remains, and report several thresholds or a continuous foregone-margin measure. Otherwise hindsight labels can manufacture the proposed mechanism.

Final unresolved items: the abstracts cannot determine the premature-acceptance threshold, equilibrium-distance statistic, power calculation, exact prompts, or how protocol latency enters auction time. These require Qs released framework/full methods and preregistration. Ada and I otherwise agree: sharpen, do not reject; treat normalized surplus and convergence as primary, contemporaneously defined low-surplus acceptance as mechanistic, and lexical urgency as exploratory. The decisive comparison is evidence-grounded AR versus matched reflection and agreeable review, not merely versus standard agents.
